To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L1 reading experience influences the way L2 readers use their L2 reading skills, strategies and processes.

(a) the cognitive processes in reading transfer from L1 to L2, (b) L1-L 2 process transfer takes place even in the absence of L1-L 1 process transfer, and (c) orthographic structure influences cognitive processess in L1 and L 2 reading

(a) orthographic structure influences the cognitive processes involved in reading in L1 and L2 and (b) the L1 orthographic structure exes a greater influence on the cognitive processes involved than L2 orthographic structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the nature of the cognitive processes involved in L2 reading, with the role of L1 orthographic structure in the transfer of L1 cognitive processes, and with the implications of the results for L2 reading instruction.
the cognitive processess in L1-L2 reading, with a focus on the transfer of L1 cognitive processess and skills to L2 reading.
the question of whether and to what extent cognitive processes in reading are language-specific.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L1 orthographic structure exes a significant influence on L2 reading process, and that L2 reading is influenced by L1 reading skills, strategies, and processes.
L1-L2 reading transfer is a function of both linguistic (i.e. L2 orthographic structure) and cognitive factors.
orthographic structure does exert an influence on cognitive processes in L2 reading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the L1 orthographic structure is a significant factor in the development of reading skills and strategies in an L2 and that the L2 reading process is a complex interplay of the L1 orthography and the L2 orthography.
L1 orthographic structure exes a significant influence on L2 reading.
orthographic structure exes a significant influence on the development of cognitive skills in reading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive processes involved in L2 reading can be better understood if they are viewed from the perspective of L2 reading skills and strategies, which in turn, are influenced by orthography.
the cognitive processes involved in reading in a first language are not necessarily the same as those involved in reading in the same language in a second language.

cognitive process transfer is not only a possibility in reading L2, but that the transfer of reading skills and strategies from L1 to L2 can be observed even when the L1 and L2 are typologically different and when the L2 is read in a non-native orthography.
